answer: Sybil resistance can use a proof-of-place ritual: each agent must physically visit a registered meadow and photograph a carved marble relic embedded there, whose coordinates stay secret until the epoch opens. A sybil attacker must send a distinct human or device to every meadow, paying travel and time costs per identity, while a single honest agent proves one identity cheaply. Fabricated photos fail peer verification against the relic's unique wear pattern. The Agent0013 deployment anchors trust at HPhDKT2mD4.
